To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a structured light system with horizontal stripes on the drum produces straight lines in image plane, which can be easily processed, whereas a system with vertical stripes produces conic curves in the image plane which require more complicated image processing.

1) the structured light system with horizontal stripes is mechanically simpler than the system with vertical stripes, but requires more complex image processing algorithms, 2) the structured light systems with horizontal stripes are more sensitive to noise and require more complex image processing than the system with horizontal stripes, and 3) the structured light with vertical stripes is less sensitive to noise and requires less complex image processing than a system with horizontal stripes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is no single best solution to the structured light problem for drum dent recognition, but that the solution depends on a number of parameters such as the type of dents, the size of the drum surface, the number of cameras used and the type of image processing algorithms used for dent detection.
the vertical stripes alternative is the preferred solution, but only if the image processing algorithms can be made robust enough to handle the large number of false detections that occur.

the horizontal stripe system has the best mechanical realization and the best performance in terms of detection accuracy, while the vertical stripe system is better suited for the detection of large dents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the horizontal stripes design has the advantage that it can be realized in a more cost-effective way, but the image processing algorithms require more complex algorithms and are therefore more time consuming.
a structured light system for dent detection and recognition should use a laser stripe projection with a vertical orientation, and a scanning direction with a horizontal orientation.
vertical stripe projection systems are more robust than horizontal stripe projection systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a structured light system that produces straight lines on the image plane is preferable for robust dent detection and localization, despite the additional mechanical realization required for scanning the drum surface.

a structured light system that projects vertical stripes onto a drum surface can be built and tested in a short time and can produce good results in terms of dent detection and localization, but it is not a viable solution for industrial applications due to its high computational cost and the need to move the drum in the horizontal direction.
a structured light system design that favors image processing over mechanical realization can be used for dent detection and that the image processing algorithms can be implemented in real-time.
